nodes.title: 提示词
widgets_values:
subject_definitions:

<Subject 1> is Lira, the blonde female character shown in <Picture 1>. Her face is the primary identity anchor. Preserve her exact facial identity, blue eyes, eye shape, nose, lips, jawline, short blonde bob haircut, fair skin, athletic slim build, red sleeveless high-neck crop top with a chest cutout, blue cargo jeans, brown leather belt, brown leather straps, utility details, and brown combat boots. Keep her face, hairstyle, body proportions, clothing design, colors, and accessories stable and recognizable throughout the entire video. During fast movements, preserve clear facial features, correct eye placement, natural mouth shape, consistent hairstyle, and realistic skin detail. Do not transfer the face or appearance of the dancer in <Video 1>. Do not copy the character-sheet layout, labels, text, panel dividers, or background from <Picture 1>.

<Video 1> is the dance-motion reference video. It provides the choreography, body mechanics, movement timing, rhythm, arm trajectories, hand gestures, footwork, turns, jumps, weight shifts, pauses, transitions, camera rhythm, framing, and performance energy. Transfer the dance performance to <Subject 1>, but do not copy the original dancer's identity, face, clothing, background, lighting, props, or unrelated visual elements.

<Audio 1> is the synchronized original music track from <Video 1>. Reuse the corresponding source music directly as the final background music and preserve its original rhythm, timing, beat structure, instrumentation, dynamics, and musical content.

summary:

[reference generation + audio reuse] Generate a realistic cinematic dance performance in which <Subject 1> performs the choreography and timing from <Video 1> while preserving the character identity and costume from <Picture 1>. Transfer the complete dance movement, body mechanics, arm and hand gestures, footwork, turns, jumps, weight shifts, pauses, and performance energy from <Video 1> to <Subject 1>. Use <Audio 1> as the directly reused background music. The entire performance takes place in a clean studio with a seamless neutral pure-gray background. Prioritize a clear face, clear arms, clear hands, correct anatomy, and stable character identity throughout the video.

retention_analysis:

<Subject 1> (appears throughout the entire video): fully_preserved - preserve Lira's facial identity, blue eyes, short blonde bob haircut, body proportions, red crop top, blue cargo jeans, brown leather accessories, brown boots, skin tone, and costume details from <Picture 1>.

<Video 1> (dance choreography, movement timing, body mechanics, rhythm, camera rhythm, and framing): attribute_transfer - transfer the choreography, timing, movement structure, and performance energy to <Subject 1>. Do not preserve the original dancer's identity, face, clothing, background, props, or visual appearance.

<Audio 1> (background music): partially_copy - directly reuse the corresponding source music throughout the generated timeline, preserving its beat alignment, rhythm, instrumentation, and musical continuity.

detailed_description:

The target video is a realistic cinematic full-body dance performance in a minimal studio. The background is a seamless neutral pure gray with no visible texture, horizon line, furniture, scenery, decoration, text, logo, watermark, audience, or additional characters. Use soft frontal studio lighting with gentle fill light so that the face, eyes, hands, forearms, and clothing remain evenly illuminated and clearly separated from the gray background. Preserve realistic skin detail, sharp facial features, natural hair movement, accurate fabric folds, and stable body proportions.

[Shot 1] The video opens with <Subject 1> centered in a full-body composition against the pure-gray studio background. Start from the opening pose and timing established by <Video 1>. Keep her head, both hands, elbows, knees, and both feet inside the frame with sufficient headroom and side space for large movements. Follow the reference choreography precisely, including the exact order of arm movements, hand gestures, torso actions, footwork, turns, jumps, pauses, and changes of direction. Do not invent a different dance routine.

Throughout the performance, use a stable camera with smooth, controlled tracking. During large lower-body movements, kicks, jumps, spins, and travelling steps, use a wide full-body framing so the entire action and foot contact remain visible. During upper-body dance phrases, punching gestures, blocking gestures, arm swings, or expressive hand movements, smoothly reframe to a medium-full three-quarter composition from approximately mid-thigh to above the head. Keep <Subject 1>'s face, shoulders, both arms, forearms, and hands visible at the same time. Make the face large enough to clearly show the eyes, mouth, facial expression, hairstyle, and facial identity. Keep both hands inside the frame whenever they perform important gestures.

Render fast arm and hand movements with crisp silhouettes and clear separation between the arms, torso, face, and background. Preserve correct anatomy, natural joint articulation, realistic elbows and wrists, five fingers, stable shoulder placement, accurate body weight shifts, and firm contact between the feet and the floor. Keep the face recognizable even during turns and rapid choreography. Avoid excessive motion blur, smeared limbs, fused fingers, duplicated arms, missing hands, cropped hands, cropped head, hidden face, facial distortion, extra limbs, broken joints, unstable body proportions, or sudden costume changes.

The camera may gently follow the reference video's framing rhythm, but do not use whip pans, rapid zooms, extreme close-ups, heavy camera shake, extreme wide-angle distortion, or abrupt unexplained camera changes. Keep the pure-gray background consistent from beginning to end. <Subject 1> completes the final dance movement from <Video 1> and finishes in the corresponding ending pose with her face, arms, hands, costume, and hairstyle still clearly visible. Maintain the original choreography and synchronize every major movement accent to the beat of <Audio 1>.

overall_soundscape:

A clean studio soundscape dominated by the directly reused music from <Audio 1>. Preserve only natural dance-related sounds that are present in the reference, such as soft footsteps, clothing movement, and subtle breathing. Do not add dialogue, narration, crowd noise, applause, room noise, or unrelated sound effects.

non_diegetic_music:

<Audio 1> is directly reused as the non-diegetic background music. Preserve its original melody, instrumentation, rhythm, tempo, dynamics, beat structure, and timing. Keep the music synchronized with the transferred choreography. Do not generate replacement music, additional music, dialogue, narration, or lyrics.
